text:
jess-support: incoming escalation from Acme (sam-acme) - multiple 502s and 'TLS handshake timeout' errors when calling Redwood hosted API eu-west endpoint since ~2026-11-02T23:02Z. Customer sees ~30% of requests fail, spikes correlated with cert rotation window. can we triage?
sam-acme: hey team - we've got a bunch of failing requests from our service -> redwood.eu-west.api:443. most requests succeed but roughly 1/3 get 502 gateway & connection errors. curl verbose shows TLS handshake that never completes. example: `curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` -> \n* Connected to api.redwood.ai (52.58.23.1) port 443 (#0)\n* TLS handshake timeout\n* Operation timed out after 600001 milliseconds with 0 out of 0 bytes received\nHTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway\n\nNo additional details on our side. started ~23:00 UTC and persists.
jess-support: thanks @sam-acme - can you paste a verbose `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.ai:443 -servername api.redwood.ai` output if you have it? also what's your resolver (company firewall / Google DNS / corporate?)
sam-acme: using internal resolver -> forwards to 8.8.8.8 through their firewall. here's tail of `openssl s_client` - it connects but then prints:
---
CONNECTED(00000003)
139789...: SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in connection to api.redwood.ai:443
sh: 0: getcwd() failed: No such file or directory
*** no peer certificate available
---
which ended with no cert chain. seems like handshake didn't complete.
mark-oncall: grabbing edge logs + metrics now. seeing spike in 502s from edge->upstream around 2026-11-02T23:01:20Z to 23:04:10Z. error summary: lots of `TLS handshake timed out` and `upstream unexpected EOF`. also seeing a small increase in resolver SERVFAIL counts. tagging infra/net.
arjun-net: quick dig/nslookup from our vantage (eu-west edge):
```
$ dig +short api.redwood.ai @127.0.0.53
52.58.23.1
52.58.23.2
```
but I also see intermittent SERVFAILs when querying customer forwarders via our health probes. forwarded queries to 8.8.8.8 fine. suspect upstream resolver path (corporate FW or intermediary) dropping EDNS0 or large UDP responses -> fallback to TCP triggers timeouts. also saw `TRUNC` occasionally.
olivia-se: timeline note: cert rotation job ran 2026-11-02T23:03:00Z for `edge-eu-west` and finished ~23:03:30Z. rotation logs show our certs were pushed successfully; cert-rotation-bot posted a summary: `cert-rotation-bot: certs rotated for edge-eu-west, new serial 0x9f3a`. however, several edge instances returned `ERR_SSL_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT` around same time. could be race between new certs + cache flush + resolver blips.
cert-rotation-bot: automated note -> cert rotation completed for edge-eu-west at 2026-11-02T23:03:30Z; thumbprint: SHA256:abcd...; rolling restart triggered for proxy processes.
jess-support: repro steps for infra team - from a VM inside same VPC as edge env run: `curl -v --resolve api.redwood.ai:443:52.58.23.1 https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health` (forces ip). when it fails, try `openssl s_client -connect 52.58.23.1:443 -servername api.redwood.ai -msg -state -tlsextdebug`. paste sample output showing handshake hanging at `ServerHello` or earlier. also capture tcpdump: `sudo tcpdump -w /tmp/handshake.pcap host 52.58.23.1 and port 443`.
arjun-net: collected tcpdump from edge host that shows repeated TCP SYN -> SYN/ACK then client to server TLS 'ClientHello' sent, server never completes handshake and eventually sends RST after retry. also saw occasional `ICMP Fragmentation needed` on path from some forwarders - indicates MTU/UDP issues that could affect EDNS0 responses. not definitive but suspicious.
mark-oncall: mitigation tried -> toggled fallback routing to route ~10% of traffic to us-west until we confirm stability. also temporarily increased upstream handshake timeout on proxies from 5s -> 10s to reduce transient 502s. early metrics: failures dropped from 30%->7% for traffic on fallback route.
olivia-se: good catch. we should also check if our cert rotation orchestration could be causing brief periods where proxies are under load (restart + reloading OCSP stapling) which combined with resolver flakiness causes handshakes to time out. can we add an extra prewarm step in the rotation (load certs before switching listeners)?
arjun-net: root cause hypothesis: combination of (1) intermittent resolver failures/EDNS truncation causing slow DNS resolution or TCP fallback delays, (2) cert rotation restarts causing a small window where proxy worker processes take longer to respond to handshakes, and (3) some corporate forwarders dropping large UDP responses -> results in client TLS attempts that time out and edge returns 502.
mark-oncall: action items done: 1) increased handshake timeout, 2) activated fallback region, 3) flushed edge DNS cache, 4) rolled back to previous cert for 2 instances to test (will reapply if stable). monitoring shows overall system recovered by 23:12Z.
pagerduty-bot: Incident #IN-20261102-2312 created: TLS handshake timeouts impacting eu-west hosted API -> ticket link https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/IN-20261102-2312 :rotating_light:
jess-support: reaching out to customer with summary and mitigation. @sam-acme can you confirm whether failures stopped for your traffic after 23:12Z?
sam-acme: confirmed - error rate dropped massively after 23:12. thanks for the quick work. do we need any action on our DNS side?
arjun-net: recommend customers using corporate forwarders to ensure EDNS0/UDP size not blocked and that forwarders allow TCP fallback. as a temporary workaround, telling them to point to public resolvers (8.8.8.8/1.1.1.1) or to increase resolver TCP/timeout settings helps. we'll add a KB doc.
olivia-se: followups: - postmortem write-up with timeline + root cause + remediation (add prewarm during cert rotations, add DNS health checks on edge probes, improve rollback automation). - add an e2e test simulating resolver truncation to catch this earlier. - add customer-facing KB recommending resolver settings.
jess-support: assigning followups: @olivia-se -> PM for postmortem, @arjun-net -> add probe and DNS test, @mark-oncall -> operationalize safe cert-rotation prewarm + rollback check. i'll update the support ticket and ping customer in the morning. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
